messages.subject: Re: R shiny bug
messages.subject_clean: R shiny bug
messages.body_plain:
It is not a shiny bug, but a problem of your code (maybe by "bug" you
meant something else). You defined mapurl as a reactive, which is
essentially a function. Then in updateSelectizeInput(), you
sprintf('code', mapurl), which certainly won't work: 1) mapurl is a
function, and sprintf() cannot accept functions as input; 2) you don't
even have %s in the first argument value of sprintf().

If you want updateSelectizeInput() to use different mapurl's according
to input$data1, you may create mapurl and update the selectize input
inside an observe() or observeEvent() like this:

  observeEvent(input$data1, {
    mapurl <- session$registerDataObj(
      ....
    )
    updateSelectizeInput(
      # use mapurl here
    )
  })

Regards,
Yihui

Uhhh I don't recommend using renderUI and htmlOutput this way. You are taking text that is fundamentally text, and coercing to HTML without escaping (meaning if the text just happens to include a string that contains special HTML characters, it could be parsed incorrectly).

How about this instead:

...
textOutput("foo"),
tags$style(type="text/css", "#foo {white-space: pre-wrap;}")
...

This should give you all the things you want. (Replace the foo in #foo with the ID of your textOutput)

messages.subject: Re: Seems like a simple problem, yet stick - editing data.frame within shinyServer
messages.subject_clean: Seems like a simple problem, yet stick - editing data.frame within shinyServer
messages.body_plain:
A couple of things here.

First:

  list <- reactiveValues()
  list = c("VTI","ARR","PJP")

<- and = are equivalent here. So you're assigning reactiveValues() to list but then immediately overwriting it with c("VTI", "ARR", "PJP"). (BTW it's probably not a great idea to have a variable named "list" anyway, given how fundamental and commonly used the list() function is in R.)

Second, I wouldn't store the data frame as a reactive value. Instead I would calculate the data frame as a reactive expression.

Third, you can't read from reactiveValues (or access the values of reactive expressions) unless you are executing within a reactive(), or an output's render expression, or in an observe() or observeEvent(). The reason for this is that if you're outside all of those contexts, then you're just executing code once, before any user interaction happens. It generally doesn't make sense to read from reactive values but then not to have a way to re-execute if those reactive values change.

Rewritten:

shinyServer(function(input,output,session){
  values <- reactiveValues(symbols = c("VTI", "ARR", "PJP"))

  df <- reactive({
    results <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
    # Be careful not to let getSymbols assign into .GlobalEnv. That could get
    # really confusing if multiple sessions are active in this Shiny app at once.
    getSymbols(values$symbols, env = results, auto.assign = TRUE)

    # I didn't know how you wanted to make the data frame, but it goes here
    data.frame(Symbol = values$symbols, ...)
  })

  output$table1 <- renderTable({ df() })
})

messages.body_plain:
I strongly disagree that one file per function is a desirable style, but to each his/her own, I suppose! A good IDE or text editor makes it very easy to jump between functions regardless of where they are (Ctrl-. In RStudio, Ctrl-P in Sublime Text).

How about having a folder in your app dir called e.g. "helpers" and then a single call in your server.R or whatever that sources everything in that directory?

    tabsetPanel(
          tabPanel('Correlation',tableOutput("corr"))
    ))
))

Server.R
data_Input <- read.csv("data.csv")

shinyServer(

      data = subset(data_Input,Category==input$category)
      cor(data[,sapply(data,is.numeric)])
    })
  }
)

Please help me fix this.

messages.subject: Re: tabPanel bug in shiny 0.12.2?
messages.subject_clean: tabPanel bug in shiny 0.12.2?
messages.body_plain:
We've changed versions of Bootstrap <http://www.getbootstrap.com/> in Shiny version 0.11, so that's probably why you're seeing different behavior. You could do something like this I believe:

tags$style(type="text/css", "#foo { overflow-x: auto; max-width: 100%; }")

Just put that before your tableOutput, and replace the "foo" in "#foo" with the id of your tableOutput (you do need the # character).

messages.subject_clean: Slow initial page-load on shiny server with long "Time to first byte"
messages.body_plain:
That's indicative of startup code taking a long time, most likely code in your global.R (if you have one) or in server.R above your server function. Consider what calculations you're doing there, and whether these calculations can be done ahead of time and cached in an .RData or (preferably) .rds file.

If you're finding even simple apps take a long time to start up, then that's not expected and you should definitely let us know.

app_idle_timeout
to a couple of days and the apps are loading quite fast now.

The weird thing was that when I browsed the apps alternating they loaded slow but when I installed Varnish (without caching as I set it up wrongly in the first try) it became fast... It still was a slow start though after waiting fore the time to the R process to terminate. Varnish is now (when correctly setup) only giving me 100-200 ms but as long as the R process is running it works great.

Best regards

Morten

Running leaflet within shinydashboard, I would like to display a shapefile representation of a road map dataset on top of a raster map from OSM.  This is to verify the closeness of fit.  But it is also to prepare to access individual polylines to visually traverse them.  Not a continuous traversal, but simulating motion of, say, 100 meters along the road at a time.

I have used readOGR() from the rgdal package, and readShapeLines() from the maptools package, to read a polyline structure from a shape file.  I see within the data structure what appears to be UTM coordinates.  How are these accessed? I am new to shapefile formats, and how they are placed into R structures.  I can get to a data frame with as.data.fram(), but that only captures the attribute data, not the location data.

Any advice how to proceed?  I can plot the shapefile object in my plot window.  AddPolyLines does not plot anything for me.  On other forums and tutorials, I do see some about how to display this data, or trim it, but I haven't seen anything about accessing the location data.  On the various geo packages, I don't see anything about traversal, identifying junctions, etc.

messages.subject: R - copy files from folder (Shiny App)
messages.subject_clean: R - copy files from folder (Shiny App)
messages.body_plain:
I'm working on loading up a Shiny App IO. I use an R package that downloads data into a subfolder in my directory and saves two .RData files.

I'm having issues on the Shiny App IO server. I need to load the two .RData files. Locally, I can set the relative path using (~project/source-data). Shiny App does not respond to this.

I can set it as a working directory using a relative path, (./source-data), however, this is not ideal as I have further data manipulation to do at the parent level directory and I can't seem to set the working directory back to the parent level in Shiny App.

Here is what I had moved forward with:
wd = getwd() sd = (paste(getwd(),"/source-data",sep="")) sd2 = list.files(sd, full.names = TRUE) file.copy(from=sd2, to=wd)

My solution, although not ideal, is to copy the two .RData files to the parent directory. At that point, the rest of my code will run smoothly. It works locally, but not on Shiny App.

Does anyone have experience with a similar problem and solution? Either helping me direct the Shiny App IO server to the sub-directory and back to the parent directory once I load in the two .RData files, or copying the files to the parent directory?

I've seen solutions that work on a local R environment, but not one that satisfies the conditions of a Shiny App IO server environment.

I asked on SO and a user suggested it's possible that there are restrictions on copying files. Is this true, and is there a workaround?

Thank you in advance.

messages.subject: debian init.d script for shiny-server
messages.subject_clean: debian init.d script for shiny-server
messages.body_plain:
I had problems with the existing init.d script for shiny-server and have made some additions and fixes.I'm pasting the diffs here, interspersed with comments in bold and am hoping most can be incorporated into the source.

Gareth

diff -Naur /apps/shiny-server/1.4.0/shiny-server/config/init.d/debian/shiny-server /etc/init.d/shiny-server
--- /apps/shiny-server/1.4.0/shiny-server/config/init.d/debian/shiny-server     2015-04-15 00:30:49.000000000 +1000
+++ /etc/init.d/shiny-server    2015-08-31 13:03:21.931666888 +1000

set some variables that might need to be customized and source a default file to override the distribution defaults
I set R and DAEMON and USERID (which could be unset for root) in /etc/default/shiny-server
PIDFILE must go in a directory that USERID can write to

@@ -19,13 +19,22 @@
 DESC="shiny server"
 NAME=shiny-server
 DAEMON=shiny-server
+USERID=shiny
+LOGDIR=/var/log/${NAME}
+LOG=${LOGDIR}/${NAME}.log
+PIDFILE=/var/run/${NAME}/${NAME}.pid
 SCRIPTNAME=/etc/init.d/shiny-server
+if [ -f /etc/default/$NAME ]; then
+       . /etc/default/$NAME
+fi
+

note that this check is busted unless DAEMON is customized to specify the full path

 # Exit if the package is not installed
 [ -x "$DAEMON" ] || exit 0

my debian setup gives no feedback if VERBOSE is not set to yes - and it gets set to no in vars.sh :-(

 # Load the VERBOSE setting and other rcS variables
 . /lib/init/vars.sh
+VERBOSE=yes

a few changes here...
options to run without root
a bit of bash to make the $LOG get written as $USERID
use shiny-server's pidfile capability to enable cleaner status and stop

 # Define LSB log_* functions.
 # Depend on lsb-base (>= 3.0-6) to ensure that this file is present.
@@ -42,7 +51,10 @@
        #   2 if daemon could not be started
        start-stop-daemon --start --quiet --background --exec $DAEMON --test > /dev/null \
                || return 1
-       start-stop-daemon --start --quiet --background --exec $DAEMON \
+       start-stop-daemon --start --background --name $NAME \
+               ${USERID:+"--user"} ${USERID:+"$USERID"} \
+               ${USERID:+"--chuid"} ${USERID:+"$USERID"} \
+               --startas /bin/bash -- -c "exec $DAEMON --pidfile=$PIDFILE >> $LOG  2>&1" \
                || return 2
 }

without this change, the service script itself would be killed on stop

@@ -56,7 +68,7 @@
        #   1 if daemon was already stopped
        #   2 if daemon could not be stopped
        #   other if a failure occurred
-       start-stop-daemon --stop --quiet --retry=TERM/30/KILL/5 --name $NAME
+       start-stop-daemon --stop --pidfile=$PIDFILE --retry=TERM/30/KILL/5 --name $NAME
        RETVAL="$?"
        [ "$RETVAL" = 2 ] && return 2
        return "$RETVAL"

adding a status option seemed a good idea

@@ -79,6 +91,9 @@
                2) [ "$VERBOSE" != no ] && log_end_msg 1 ;;
        esac
        ;;
+  status)
+       status_of_proc -p $PIDFILE $DAEMON $NAME
+       ;;
   restart|force-reload)
        log_daemon_msg "Restarting $DESC" "$NAME"
        do_stop

messages.subject: Cleaner and better code with the backpipe package
messages.subject_clean: Cleaner and better code with the backpipe package
messages.body_plain:
Hi all, I have wrote the backpipe package that I believe will make Shiny code more readable, more debuggable, more maintainable and clearer. If you love magrittr and pipeR, you may have been frustrated using it to write shiny code. Let's say you are doing something like this: h1( "content", role="heading" ) %>% div( class="inner") %>% div( class="outer") %>% div( class="outer-outer") This produces valid HTML:

content

but illustrates two incongruities between code and output. The First is the reversal of order between code and output. This makes it hard to debug the generated HTML. The second problems is that code indentation no longer illustrate the nested structure of the output. Using the backpipe operator the same code can be written as: library(backpipe) div( class="outer-outer") %<% div( class="outer") %<% div( class="inner") %<% h1( "content", role="heading" ) Now operation order and code better matches the generated HTML output. I hope this helps for the larger Shiny projects. I would appreciate any feedback you have. Thanks, Chris

messages.subject_clean: How to make a for loop reactive in shiny server?
messages.body_plain:
If you mean, make the code react to a user input for number of variables, then all you need to do is create an input widget for the user to select the number of variables. Either a sliderInput or numericInput or selectInput will do.

Then, you won't need m <- reactive({1:5}). You can just have your loop reference the input like this: for(i in 1:input$number){ your code }.

As for making the variables accessible by other functions, you should be able to use the envir argument of assign() to scope it to a different environment that's more accessible. Try envir = globalnenv().

messages.body_plain:
When h1/h2 change, do you want output$b to update? If so, these are not normal variables but reactive values.

server <- function(input, output) {

  m <- reactive({1:5})

  v <- reactiveValues()

  output$a <- renderPrint({

    for (i in 1:length(m())){

      v[[paste0("h",i)]] <- "u"
    }

    list(v$h1,v$h2)
  })

  output$b <- renderPrint({

   list(v$h1,v$h2)

  })
}
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

messages.body_plain:
I have a shinydashboard application that includes rendering leaflet widgets.  I want to do some "walking through the map" things.  That is, on a timed basis, I want to draw a polyline on the map that keeps extending every so many seconds, with a circleMarker on the end.  The user can select the direction of movement and the speed of movement.

I have experimented with reactivePoll, but where does that go?  Inside an observe function?  I saw an example at Rstudio.com of using invalidateLater as a timer, but I don't see how to apply that.  Or are reactiveValues useful here?

I am attaching the server.R code.  Thanks for any help you can give.  Would like to make progress on this quickly.

messages.subject: Re: Timing function in leaflet/shinydashboard application
messages.subject_clean: Timing function in leaflet/shinydashboard application
messages.body_plain:
The general pattern would be something like this:

observe({
  invalidateLater(1000, session)
  isolate({
    # Code goes here...
  })
})

The code at "# Code goes here" will execute once per 1000 milliseconds (the first time is at session start, not session start plus 1000 milliseconds).

If you want to mutate a path, then maybe something like this:

v <- reactiveValues(
  lastPoint = c(lat = 0, lng = 0),
  path = data.frame(lat = numeric(0), lng = numeric(0))
)

observe({
  invalidateLater(1000, session)
  isolate({
    deltaLat <- 1
    deltaLng <- 1
    v$lastPoint <- v$lastPoint + c(lat = deltaLat, lng = deltaLng)
    v$path <- rbind(v$path, v$lastPoint)
  })
})

observe({
  leafletProxy("map", v$path) %>% addPolylines(layerId = "path")
})

messages.body_plain:
Nice idea, thank you. My first reaction when I was reading your text was "I never use or seen people use magirttr pipes in shiny code". I suppose the reason I never even thought of doing it is because of how you have to write the HTML backwards as you mentioned. It would help if you maybe also compare the native Shiny way of writing the same code div(class="outer-outer", div(class="outer", div(class="inner", h1("content", role="heading") ) ) ) It's easier to compare this version to your backpipe version, and every Shiny developer understands this code. It honestly took me a minute to understand the magrittr version. On Friday, 4 September 2015 04:52:24 UTC-7, cbr...@decisionpatterns.com wrote: > Hi all, > > I have wrote the backpipe package that I believe will make Shiny code more readable, more debuggable, more maintainable and clearer. If you love magrittr and pipeR, you may have been frustrated using it to write shiny code. Let's say you are doing something like this: > > h1( "content", role="heading" ) %>% > div( class="inner") %>% > div( class="outer") %>% > div( class="outer-outer") > > > This produces valid HTML: > > >
>
>
>

content

>
>
>
> > but illustrates two incongruities between code and output. The First is the reversal of order between code and output. This makes it hard to debug the generated HTML. The second problems is that code indentation no longer illustrate the nested structure of the output. Using the backpipe operator the same code can be written as: > > > > library(backpipe) > > div( class="outer-outer") %<% > div( class="outer") %<% > div( class="inner") %<% > h1( "content", role="heading" ) > > Now operation order and code better matches the generated HTML output. > > I hope this helps for the larger Shiny projects. I would appreciate any feedback you have. > > Thanks, > > Chris >

messages.subject_clean: IE iframe error on simple app; Firefox, Chrome have no errors...
messages.body_plain:
This simple app (very bottom) illustrates some significant issues I am seeing with IE and Shiny Server. These issues do not appear with local Shiny via RStudio. Shiny 0.12.0, Shiny Server 1.3.0.403 Using the below app.R, I see this in the IE Console: SCRIPT5: Access is denied. File: iframe.html, Line: 1, Column: 1 The message is in IE only, it doesn't appear in other browsers like Chrome or Firefox. While this example still renders, more complex examples won't due to similar messages in IE (once again, no errors in other browsers.) Here's where it's links to when I click through the error:

Don't panic!

This is a SockJS hidden iframe. It's used for cross domain magic.

# Begin app.R library(shiny) library(leaflet) r_colors <- rgb(t(col2rgb(colors()) / 255)) names(r_colors) <- colors() ui <- fluidPage( leafletOutput("mymap"), p(), actionButton("recalc", "New points") ) server <- function(input, output, session) { points <- eventReactive(input$recalc, { cbind(rnorm(40) * 2 + 13, rnorm(40) + 48) }, ignoreNULL = FALSE) output$mymap <- renderLeaflet({ leaflet() %>% addProviderTiles("Stamen.TonerLite", options = providerTileOptions(noWrap = TRUE) ) %>% addMarkers(data = points()) }) } shinyApp(ui, server) # End app.R

Hi,

I've gone through all threads on "Shiny.onInputChange" so hopefully I'm not duplicating a question.

I'm building a shiny app with some extra d3 graphing capability implemented through htmlwidgets. Following this tutorial <https://ryouready.wordpress.com/2013/11/20/sending-data-from-client-to-server-and-back-using-shiny/> I was easily able to implement addCustomMessageHandler for sending messages from R to my js library. The other direction seems to be more tricky. I'm trying to add a listener to a label on a line graph and send a message to R reporting the position of the label. The d3 listener works fine (I can see that through console.log) so I tried to add Shiny.onInputChange to the listeners function but its not working.

I draw the graph only after loading data which is sent through a dialog. Is it possible that at this point (drawing the graph) it is too late to register the input variable which is the first argument of the Shiny.onInputChange function? If so, can I register it somehow sooner without having the data initialised?

Thanks for any hints and pointer.

Karol

Hi all,

I also encountered this issue and found this post, but unfortunately couldn't replicate the workaround successfully.

    df1 <-

      output$txt1 <- renderText({
        df1 %>% summarise(y1 = mean(input$select,na.rm = T)) %>%

      })

      width = 3,
      selectInput(
        "select", label = h3("Variable"),
        choices = list("long name 1" = "long name 1",

      )

    mainPanel(h3(textOutput(
      "txt1"
    )))))

    shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

The only solution that I can think is to use a series of if statements instead of using input$select directly in summarise. Any suggestions?

messages.body_plain:
I believe the problem is in the `deltamethod` function from the msm package.

It contains this code:
    gdashmu <- t(sapply(g, function(form) {
        as.numeric(attr(eval(deriv(form, syms)), "gradient"))
    }))

The part that's throwing the error (I think) is the `eval(deriv(form, syms))`. I think the `eval()` is not respecting the source environment where `deltamethod` is called from. This isn't a problem in interactive R use, because most of your stuff lives in the Global environment, and these functions will automatically search there. But this fails with Shiny because Shiny's environment structure is different. I believe it would also fail if you called deltamethod from another package and expected it to find variables that lived in that package.

Here's some example code to illustrate:

# Create a new environment, and give it a value for x
e <- new.env()
e$x <- 1
e
# <environment: 0xdc4d668>

# Create a formula with that environment
f <- evalq(~ x^2, envir = e)
str(f)
# Class 'formula' length 2 ~x^2
#   ..- attr(*, ".Environment")=<environment: 0xdc4d668>

# This returns an expression
deriv(f, "x")
# expression({
#     .value <- x^2
#     .grad <- array(0, c(length(.value), 1L), list(NULL, c("x")))
#     .grad[, "x"] <- 2 * x
#     attr(.value, "gradient") <- .grad
#     .value
# })

# But we can't evaluate that expression in the current (global) envrionment,
# because `x` isn't defined here.
eval(deriv(f, "x"))
# Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) : object 'x' not found

# We need to evaluate it in environment e
eval(deriv(f, "x"), envir = e)
# [1] 1
# attr(,"gradient")
#      x
# [1,] 2

I believe the best solution is to modify `deltamethod` so that it captures the calling environment (using parent.frame())`, and passes that to the eval. This is something that the msm authors would need to address. It would be something like this:

deltamethod <- function (g, mean, cov, ses = TRUE, envir = parent.frame()) {
    ....
    gdashmu <- t(sapply(g, function(form) {
        as.numeric(attr(eval(deriv(form, syms), envir = e), "gradient"))
    }))
    ....
}

-Winston

messages.body_plain:
You can use the `summarise_` function when you want to use variables in dplyr functions. Other dplyr functions also have a version with a trailing underscore. For example:

library(dplyr)

# The usual way of using dplyr
mtcars %>%
  group_by(cyl) %>%
  summarise(meanwt = mean(wt))

# Passing in strings in variables
group <- "cyl"
var <- "mean(wt)"
mtcars %>%
  group_by_(group) %>%
  summarise_(meanwt = var)

See https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/dplyr/vignettes/nse.html for more information.

and in my server, r

# Load the dataset
loadData <- function() {
  df <- read.csv("./data/tab1.csv")
  return(df)
}

# Get bar chart
getBar <- function(df, reaction){
  sex <- reaction$sex
  if (sex == "M") {
    indices <- which(df$Sex == "M")
    new_df <- df[indices, ]
    p <- ggplot(data = new_df, aes(x = Age, y = Percent, fill = factor(Year))) + geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge())
    p
  }

    indices <- which(df$Sex == "F")
    new_df <- df[indices, ]
    p <- ggplot(data = new_df, aes(x = Age, y = Percent, fill = factor(Year))) + geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge())
    p
  }
}

##### GLOBAL OBJECTS #####

# Shared data
globalData <- loadData()

##### SHINY SERVER #####
# Create shiny server.
shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  cat("Press \"ESC\" to exit...\n")
  # Copy the data frame
  localFrame <- globalData

  getReaction1 <- reactive({
    return(list(
                sex = input$sex
    ))
  }) # getReaction1

  # Output Plots.
output$bar <- renderPlot({print(getBar(localFrame, getReaction1()))}) # output bar

  }) # shinyServer

df <- read.csv("./data/tab1.csv")

p <- ggplot(data = new_df, aes(x = Age, y = Percent, fill = factor(Year))) + geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge())
p

but doesn't show nothing inside dashboard

Can you please show what I am doing wrong

Regards

messages.subject: Error when trying to deploy to shinyapps.io: Application depends on package "package" but it is not
messages.subject_clean: Error when trying to deploy to shinyapps.io: Application depends on package "package" but it is not
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

My server.R contains the following code for dynamically installing packages when needed:

package <- input$chip

if (!require(package, character.only=T, quietly=T)) {
      source("https://bioconductor.org/biocLite.R")
      biocLite(package, ask = F, suppressUpdates = T, suppressAutoUpdate = T)
      library(package, character.only=T)
    }

ui.R has a select input element where the user can select one of the following:

selectInput(inputId = 'chip', label='Chip', choices=c('Mouse Gene 1.0'='mogene10sttranscriptcluster.db',
                                                      'Mouse Gene 2.0'='mogene20sttranscriptcluster.db',
                                                      'Human Gene 1.0'='hugene10sttranscriptcluster.db',
                                                      'Human Genome U133A 2.0'='hgu133a2.db'))

So, based on what chip the user selects,  the corresponding annotation package should get loaded, and if not installed, it should install it.

This works on my local machine. But when I try to deploy my app on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>. I get the following error:

Error:
* Application depends on package "package" but it is not installed. Please resolve before continuing.

I know that it is unable to recognize the 'package' in biocLite(package, ask = F, suppressUpdates = T, suppressAutoUpdate = T).  Is there any way to resolve this? Or do I have to explicitly load all required packages?
The problem is that annotation packages are so big they take up a lot of memory, which is why I wanted to load these packages only when required.

An alternative is to make an if-else loop or switch statement to install packages based on the condition, but I just wanted to know if this can work because this is so concise.

Thanks!

To see if this is indeed the issue, maybe try deploying something simple such as

mypkg <- "ggplot2"
library(mypkg , character.only = TRUE)

If that gives an error of "unable to deploy package 'mypkg'", then it's definitely a bug

Hi Winston,
Thank you much for looking at this indeed defining the deltamethod as below solved the problem.
What was weird is that it worked as is before the latest shiny release but with this fix I will be sure that it will work in the future.
Bests,
Samer

deltamethod <- function (g, mean, cov, ses = TRUE, envir = parent.frame())
{

    cov <- as.matrix(cov)
    n <- length(mean)
    if (!is.list(g))
        g <- list(g)
    if ((dim(cov)[1] != n) || (dim(cov)[2] != n))
        stop(paste("Covariances should be a ", n, " by ", n,
            " matrix"))
    syms <- paste("x", 1:n, sep = "")
    for (i in 1:n) assign(syms[i], mean[i])
    gdashmu <- t(sapply(g, function(form) {
        as.numeric(attr(eval(deriv(form, syms), envir = envir), "gradient"))
    }))
    new.covar <- gdashmu %*% cov %*% t(gdashmu)
    if (ses) {
        new.se <http://new.se> <- sqrt(diag(new.covar))
        new.se <http://new.se>
    }
    else new.covar
}

On Wed, Sep 9, 2015 at 12:53 PM, Winston Chang <win...@rstudio.com> wrote:
> I believe the problem is in the `deltamethod` function from the msm package.
>
> It contains this code:
>     gdashmu <- t(sapply(g, function(form) {
>         as.numeric(attr(eval(deriv(form, syms)), "gradient"))
>     }))
>
>
> The part that's throwing the error (I think) is the `eval(deriv(form, syms))`. I think the `eval()` is not respecting the source environment where `deltamethod` is called from. This isn't a problem in interactive R use, because most of your stuff lives in the Global environment, and these functions will automatically search there. But this fails with Shiny because Shiny's environment structure is different. I believe it would also fail if you called deltamethod from another package and expected it to find variables that lived in that package.
>
> Here's some example code to illustrate:
>
>
> # Create a new environment, and give it a value for x
> e <- new.env()
> e$x <- 1
> e
> # <environment: 0xdc4d668>
>
> # Create a formula with that environment
> f <- evalq(~ x^2, envir = e)
> str(f)
> # Class 'formula' length 2 ~x^2
> #   ..- attr(*, ".Environment")=<environment: 0xdc4d668>
>
>
> # This returns an expression
> deriv(f, "x")
> # expression({
> #     .value <- x^2
> #     .grad <- array(0, c(length(.value), 1L), list(NULL, c("x")))
> #     .grad[, "x"] <- 2 * x
> #     attr(.value, "gradient") <- .grad
> #     .value
> # })
>
>
> # But we can't evaluate that expression in the current (global) envrionment,
> # because `x` isn't defined here.
> eval(deriv(f, "x"))
> # Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) : object 'x' not found
>
>
> # We need to evaluate it in environment e
> eval(deriv(f, "x"), envir = e)
> # [1] 1
> # attr(,"gradient")
> #      x
> # [1,] 2
>
>
>
> I believe the best solution is to modify `deltamethod` so that it captures the calling environment (using parent.frame())`, and passes that to the eval. This is something that the msm authors would need to address. It would be something like this:
>
> deltamethod <- function (g, mean, cov, ses = TRUE, envir = parent.frame()) {
>     ....
>     gdashmu <- t(sapply(g, function(form) {
>         as.numeric(attr(eval(deriv(form, syms), envir = e), "gradient"))
>     }))
>     ....
> }
>
>
> -Winston

messages.subject: R shiny leaflet maps do not load for more than one browser instance
messages.subject_clean: R shiny leaflet maps do not load for more than one browser instance
messages.body_plain:
We're creating a webapp (http://52.2.13.97:3838/Boston-Inspections/) that uses a `leaflet` map. `shiny-server` is being run on an Amazon EC2 Ubuntu instance. The code for the webapp can be found on the github: https://github.com/jkgenser/Boston-Inspections

We noticed (and you can probably notice from the link) that the map does not update as it should when the `shiny` inputs change. However, they do update for the very first instance of `shiny` on the EC2 instance.

Does anyone know why the map would properly render for the very instance, but for every subsequent instance, the map simply does not load/update? If it helps, all of these 'instances' seem to run in the same worker process on the EC2 instance (ie. multiple tabs running the webapp will all be contained under the same process via `ps aux`). We suspect it might have something to do with leaflet only rendering once per shiny process, so when one user controls that process, they control the rendering but no other user who opens the webapp can have their leaflet map re-render and update. We’d greatly appreciate if you have any insight into this.

Thanks for any insights you can offer!

messages.body_plain:
Well, the shinyapps server that runs your code must install all the used libraries during deployment. They don't want to have to do dynamic package installation. So you do need to let shinyapps know about all the potential packages it needs when you deploy.

It sounds like your issue could be linked with this one
https://github.com/rstudio/shinyapps/issues/167

If there was a ShinySuggests field in the DESCRIPTION then you could list all the potential packages there without changing your code

---

If you love magrittr and pipeR, you may have been frustrated using it to write shiny code. Let's say you are doing something like this: > > > > h1( "content", role="heading" ) %>% > > div( class="inner") %>% > > div( class="outer") %>% > > div( class="outer-outer") > > > > > > This produces valid HTML: > > > > > >
> >
> >
> >

content

> >
> >
> >
> > > > but illustrates two incongruities between code and output. The First is the reversal of order between code and output. This makes it hard to debug the generated HTML. messages.body_plain:
It's surprising that just this one app would show this message. But if the app is otherwise working fine, it's not anything to worry about. We use a library called SockJS to manage communication between the browser and Shiny Server, and that library will try to use different transport mechanisms including websockets; if it can't use websockets it is supposed to move onto a different mechanism gracefully.

messages.subject: How does Shiny handles data in app.R?
messages.subject_clean: How does Shiny handles data in app.R?
messages.body_plain:
I have gone through Shiny tutorials. I understand that if you design your app such that there are separate ui.R, server.R and global.R and you read the data in global.R, Shiny would first read it and then use it according to server.R.
But what about app.R? If I have a `df` in global environment and I want to access the app for local use only, what is the most efficient (fastest) way to access the data? Should I put something like following at the top in app.R?

# Global
df <- read.csv('dfcf.csv')

Can I somehow tell Shiny that `df` is already in the global environment and it doesn't have to read it in? I am concerned because my data size is more than 1 GB and the app takes long to read it in. Sorry, if the question is too naive. I am still learning.

messages.subject_clean: How does Shiny handles data in app.R?
messages.body_plain:
Yeah, right at the top is fine.

You can do something like this:

if (!exists("df")) {

  df <- read.csv('dfcf.csv')
}

By the way, also check out the readr package, or the data.table package's fread function. Both of them are dramatically faster than read.csv.

messages.subject: Re: DT addRow Uses Duplicate Row Names
messages.subject_clean: DT addRow Uses Duplicate Row Names
messages.body_plain:
Row names is only a concept in R. DataTables does not have this
concept, and "row names" are only a column in the table, so it does
not matter if there are any duplicates. In the addRow example, the new
row is a random row in the existing data, so the row name will be
duplicated. In your own application, you are free to use new row
names.

Regards,
Yihui

messages.body_plain:
The issue has to do with the way R is installed on the server.  According to the instruction found here <https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-server/wiki/Ubuntu-step-by-step-install-instructions> on rstudio wiki on github, R was installed under an ubuntu user who was logged in at the time, prior to shiny installation and shiny user creation.  The shiny server admin guide here  <http://rstudio.github.io/shiny-server/latest/#installation>doesn't also specify how to install R so that it is available to ALL users.

This fixed my problem I run the following command to install tm package for "all" R user
sudo su - -c "R -e \"install.packages('tm', repos='http://cran.rstudio.com/')\""

But to avoid the headache for others and have the correct procedure in place on gitbuh/admin guide, it is better to add a global R installation step prior shiny server installation.

-G

messages.subject: Re: Small issue with the way reactivity works
messages.subject_clean: Small issue with the way reactivity works
messages.body_plain:
Yeah, non deterministic actions don't work as well with our style of reactivity. Call it a known limitation with an easy workaround. :)

On Fri, Sep 11, 2015 at 4:30 PM Dean Attali <daat...@gmail.com> wrote:

> I just answered a SO question <http://stackoverflow.com/questions/32519406/modifying-a-reactive-value-should-trigger-an-observe-chunk> which made me realize a small issue with the way reactivity works. Consider the following code
>
> shinyApp(
>   ui = fluidPage(
>     actionButton("btn", "button")
>   ),
>   server = function(input, output, session) {
>     rv = reactiveValues(counter = 0)
>
>     observeEvent(input$btn, {
>       cat("pressed button\n")
>       rv$counter <- rv$counter + 1
>     })
>
>     observe({
>       if (runif(1) < 0.5) {
>         cat("counter value: ", rv$counter, "\n")
>       }
>     })
>   }
> )
>
> We have a reactiveValues counter that gets updated every time the action button is clicked. We have an observer that observes that prints the value of the counter but it only prints it half the times, using a random number generator.  Because of the way reactive dependencies are determines, this code doesn't actually work the way you'd naively expect. Only 50% of the times the observer knows that the counter is a dependency, and with every successive iteration, again there's a 50% chance the dependency won't be picked up.
>
> I understand why this happens, I'm just wondering if this is the theoretically correct behaviour, or is this just a weird unwanted side effect of reactivity?
>
> Of course a simple workaround would be to make a dummy call to the counter in the observer so that it'll always be a dependency, or to use observeEvent, but it's more a theoretical question.
>

messages.subject: Linking zoom or pan across leaflet plots in Shiny.
messages.subject_clean: Linking zoom or pan across leaflet plots in Shiny.
messages.body_plain:
I have a set of two leaflet plots that are intended to represent the same area of interest, but with different raster layers.  I would like to lock the two leaflet panels in a way so that changing the extent of one changes the extent of the other.

Currently, in my server.R file I am using renderLeaflet to create the two panels, and then using 'observe' to modify the plots based on user inputs from the side-bar.

Here is a minimal example:

server.R:

shinyServer(function(input,output){
  dataset1 <- reactive({

    sub_raster <- raster(xmn=-98.6,xmx=-66.1,ymn=36.5,ymx=49.75,
                         crs="+init=epsg:4326", resolution = 0.0833333)
    return(list(mean = setValues(sub_raster, ncell(sub_raster):1),
                sds  = setValues(sub_raster, 1:ncell(sub_raster)))
    })

  output$MapPlot<-renderLeaflet({
    map <- leaflet() %>% addProviderTiles("Esri.WorldImagery") %>%
      fitBounds(lng1=-98.6,lng2=-66.1,lat1=36.5,lat2=49.75)

  })

  output$MapPlot2<-renderLeaflet({
    map <- leaflet() %>% addProviderTiles("Esri.WorldImagery") %>%
      fitBounds(lng1=-98.6,lng2=-66.1,lat1=36.5,lat2=49.75)

  })

  observe({
    leafletProxy("MapPlot") %>%
      clearImages() %>%
      addRasterImage(layerId = "ds1Mean",
                     dataset1()$mean,
                     opacity = input$transparancy)
    leafletProxy("MapPlot2") %>%
      clearImages() %>%
      addRasterImage(layerId = "ds1SD",
                     dataset1()$sds,
                     opacity = input$transparancy)
  })

})

ui.R:
library(shiny)

shinyUI(fluidPage(
  # Application title:
  titlePanel("Minimal Example"),

  # Sidebar with dropdown choice of taxa:
  sidebarPanel(
    sliderInput(inputId = "transparancy",
                  label = "Transparancy:",
                  min = 0.0, max = 1, value = 0.5, step = 0.05),
    width = 2),

  mainPanel(fluidRow(
    column(5,leafletOutput("MapPlot")),
    column(5,leafletOutput("MapPlot2"))
    )))
  )

Does anyone have any thoughts?  If worst comes to worst I could probably move the zoom/pan into the sidebar panel, but I'd rather not.

messages.subject: Re: Does shiny server function def params HAVE to be named "input" "output" and "session"?
messages.subject_clean: Does shiny server function def params HAVE to be named "input" "output" and "session"?
messages.body_plain:
Hey Joe,

I don't fully understand the 'getDefaultReactiveDomain' and the idea of having different reactive domains. I guess I just never explicitly had to use more than one?  Anyway, the question I actually need help with is: can I get the shiny session object using getDefaultReactiveDomain from within one of the session callback functions, such as session$onFlush()?

Example:

foo <- function() {
  cat(str(getDefaultReactiveDomain()))
}

shinyApp(
  ui = fluidPage(),

  server = function(input, output, session) {

    foo()
    session$onFlush(foo)
  }
)

The first time it prints the shiny session, the second time it prints NULL. How can I access the shiny session inside foo?

On Thursday, 23 July 2015 20:36:32 UTC-7, Dean Attali wrote:
> Thanks Joe, I was actually planning on asking you what's the right way to do this -- this is much better
>
> On Thursday, 23 July 2015 18:46:52 UTC-7, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
> > Don't go looking for the session object--use getDefaultReactiveDomain(). If it returns an object, it's a Shiny session; if it returns NULL, you're being called in a context that wasn't set up by a Shiny session (for example, an observer that was defined outside of the server function).
> >
> > On Thu, Jul 23, 2015 at 4:51 PM Dean Attali <daat...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > Ok cool, just needed to know.  In shinyjs the internal functions automatically look for the session object so I just thought that if users can call it something else, I would need to support that as well, but it's easier this way.
> > >
> > >
> > > On Thursday, 23 July 2015 16:39:29 UTC-7, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
> > > > Yeah, it's currently necessary.
> > > > https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/a47a690a68f414d3975c2ad9e841d705b03489fd/R/server.R#L296-L310
> > > >
> > > > Especially for session, since we used to have a clientData parameter in that position (which is now deprecated but it still works).
> > > >
> > > > It'd be easy enough to make input/output work with other names, but I thought it was good for the community if everyone used the same names anyway.
> > > > On Thu, Jul 23, 2015 at 2:05 PM, Dean Attali <daat...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > I know that the conventional way to define the shiny server function is
> > > > >
> > > > > server = function(input, output, session) {}
> > > > >
> > > > > I noticed that if I try to change the param names to other names, bad things happen.  Is it expected that we should only use these specific names, and no other name can be used for the params?  I know everywhere I look I see these names being used but I didn't see anywhere that explicitly said that you cannot change the param names, so I just want to get confirmation

Warning: Unhandled error in observer: object 'vals' not found
observeEvent(input$plot1_click)

Here is my data, saved as a tab delimited text file:

"conc"    "intensity"
    1    2.07333369724137
    2    2.4529660334807
    3    0.2
    4    7.67415236417532
    5    10.2760669593536
    6    13.1542128315895
    7    12.6869121113782
    8    16.2577553453706
    9    19.7970127998953
   10    19.4761527186236

Here is my code:

library(shiny)
library(ggplot2)

ui <- fluidPage(
sidebarLayout(
  sidebarPanel(
    h2("File Picker"),
    fileInput("file", "Choose a data file"),
    br(),
    textOutput("filename"),
    textOutput("text56"),
    br(),
    tableOutput("table1")
  ),
  mainPanel(
    plotOutput("plot1", click = "plot1_click",
               brush = brushOpts(id = "plot1_brush")),
    actionButton("viewPlot", "View Plot"),
    actionButton("exclude_toggle", "Toggle points"),
    actionButton("exclude_reset", "Reset")
  )
)
)

server <- function(input, output){
  # browser()
  output$filename <- renderText({
    if(is.null(input$file)) return(NULL)
    input$file$name
  })

  mydata <-  reactive({
    if(is.null(input$file)) return(NULL)
    read.table(input$file$datapath, header = TRUE, sep = "\t")
  })

  output$table1 <- renderTable({
    if (is.null(input$file)) return(NULL)
    mydata()
  })

  observeEvent(input$viewPlot, handlerExpr = {
    if(!is.null(input$file)){
      df <- isolate(mydata())
      vals <- reactiveValues(
        keeprows = if(!is.null(df)) rep(TRUE, nrow(df))
      )
      output$plot1 <- renderPlot({
        #       if(is.null(mydata())) return(NULL)
        #       if(is.null(vals$keeprows)) return(NULL)
        df <- mydata()
        mynames <- names(df)

        # Plot the kept and excluded points as two separate data sets
        keep    <- df[ vals$keeprows, , drop = FALSE]
        exclude <- df[!vals$keeprows, , drop = FALSE]

        p <- ggplot(keep, aes_string(x = mynames[1], y = mynames[2]))
        p + geom_point() +
          geom_smooth(method = lm, fullrange = TRUE, shape = 21, color = "black") +
          geom_point(data = exclude, shape = 21, fill = NA, color = "black",
                     alpha = 0.25)
      })
    }
  }, ignoreNULL = TRUE)

  # Toggle points that are clicked
  observeEvent(input$plot1_click, {
    res <- nearPoints(df, input$plot1_click, allRows = TRUE)
    vals$keeprows <- xor(vals$keeprows, res$selected_)

  })

}

The entire "observeEvent(input$viewPlot..." section is incorrect, sorry. The correct code is much simpler. Revert your server function back to the example, and replace all the mtcars references with mydata(), and declare the mydata <- reactive(...) to handle your upload.

If you don't want to view the plot immediately but wait until View Plot is clicked, then you can use an eventReactive:

delayed_mydata <- eventReactive(input$viewPlot, {
  mydata())
})

and then in your renderPlot or wherever else you want to delay updating until the button is clicked, refer to delayed_mydata() instead of mydata().

Hope that helps.

Thanks, Joe.  Your explanation confirms my nascent understanding of how shiny is supposed to work.  I have changed the code below to adopt your suggestions--now it is the same as the example code but tweaked to include a fileInput ui.  Also, I dropped the library call to Cairo, which fails on my system and which I don't believe is important.

Unfortunately, I get a new error when I run the code:  Error: Line starting '<!DOCTYPE html> ...' is malformed!  From googling a bit this seems to have something to do with R referencing webpages that don't exist.  I tried splitting the code into independent ui.R and server.R files, and that fixed the problem...no idea why.

However, once the app runs I get a different error which seems to crop up all the time (perhaps because I don't understand reactivity completely):

Error in .getReactiveEnvironment()$currentContext() :
  Operation not allowed without an active reactive context. (You tried to do something that can only be done from inside a reactive expression or observer.)

By experimentation, I discovered that the source of the error seems to be the statement assigning vals, and, more specifically, the command nrow(mydata()).  If I comment out nrow(mydata()) as shown below and stick in a number, no error occurs, and the app runs.  (Of course, there are problems with 12 not actually being the correct number of rows, but that's a side issue)

    keeprows = rep(TRUE, 12) #nrow(mydata()))
  )

On the other hand, if I comment out the vals assignment completely, the rest of the script can't do its job and I get an error that I expect:

Error in func() : object 'vals' not found
Error in `[.data.frame`(mydata(), vals$keeprows, , drop = FALSE) :
  object 'vals' not found

Any further insights?  My version of shiny is 0.12.2, by the way, and R version 3.1.2 (2014-10-31).

Ted

Revised code below:
#########################################

library(shiny)
library(ggplot2)

ui <- fluidPage(

  fluidRow(
    column(width = 6,
  fileInput("file", "Load File"),
                    plotOutput("plot1", height = 350,

                      click = "plot1_click",
                      brush = brushOpts(
                        id = "plot1_brush"
                      )

           ),
           actionButton("exclude_toggle", "Toggle points"),
           actionButton("exclude_reset", "Reset")
    )
  )
)

server <- function(input, output) {

  mydata <- reactive({
    if(!is.null(input$file)){

      read.table(input$file$datapath, header = TRUE, sep = "\t")
    }
  })

  # For storing which rows have been excluded
  vals <- reactiveValues(
    keeprows = rep(TRUE, nrow(mydata()))
  )

  output$plot1 <- renderPlot({
    mynames <- names(mydata())

    # Plot the kept and excluded points as two separate data sets

    keep    <- mydata()[ vals$keeprows, , drop = FALSE]
    exclude <- mydata()[!vals$keeprows, , drop = FALSE]

    ggplot(keep, aes_string(mynames[1], mynames[2])) +

      geom_point() +
      geom_smooth(method = lm, fullrange = TRUE, shape = 21, color = "black") +
      geom_point(data = exclude, shape = 21, fill = NA, color = "black", alpha = 0.25)

  })

  # Toggle points that are clicked
  observeEvent(input$plot1_click, {

    res <- nearPoints(mydata(), input$plot1_click, allRows = TRUE)

    vals$keeprows <- xor(vals$keeprows, res$selected_)
  })

  # Toggle points that are brushed, when button is clicked
  observeEvent(input$exclude_toggle, {
    res <- brushedPoints(mydata(), input$plot1_brush, allRows = TRUE)

    vals$keeprows <- xor(vals$keeprows, res$selected_)
  })

  # Reset all points
  observeEvent(input$exclude_reset, {
    vals$keeprows <- rep(TRUE, nrow(mydata()))
  })

}

shinyApp(ui, server)

##server file

library(shiny)
library(shinydashboard)

shinyServer(function(input,output,session) {

  output$ui <- renderUI({
    eval(parse(system.file("examples/01_hello/ui.R", package="shiny")))
  })
  subserver <- eval(parse(system.file("examples/01_hello/server.R", package="shiny")))
  subserver(input,output)

})

##ui.R
library(shiny)
library(shinydashboard)

shinyUI(dashboardPage(
  ## HEADER
  dashboardHeader(title="",
                  titleWidth = 335),

  dashboardSidebar(
    width = 335
  ),
  dashboardBody(
    htmlOutput('ui')
  )

))

you can create inputs which change the location of the app ui and server locations this way and handle everything in the server controller

messages.subject: Re: Trouble accessing uploaded data frame
messages.subject_clean: Trouble accessing uploaded data frame
messages.body_plain:
Sorry for the delay, I'm on vacation.

  vals <- reactiveValues(
    keeprows = rep(TRUE, 12) #nrow(mydata()))
  )

What's your intention with this code? Is keeprows supposed to stay up to date as mydata changes? Or is it supposed to just run a single time at startup? If so, at the time this code is running, are you sure mydata() is going to return something sensible (I suspect not as mydata requires a file upload)?

I'll assume that you want to prepopulate keeprows each time a new file is uploaded. Then you'll do something like this:

vals <- reactiveValues(
  keeprows = NULL
)
observe({

  vals$keeprows <- rep(TRUE, nrow(mydata()))
})

Also add this line to the beginning of the mydata reactive:

validate(need(input$file, FALSE))

The validate/need call will cause any code that calls mydata() to silently/cleanly abort if the file hasn't been uploaded yet (i.e. your outputs will be blank, without any error).

The observer will cause keeprows to stay up to date.

The one edge case you may still hit, is if an observer or renderXXX accesses vals$keeprows without first accessing mydata(). You can either check for NULL in those cases (or better yet, validate(need(vals$keeprows, FALSE)) ) or wrap the access to vals$keeprows in a reactive that calls validate(need(vals$keeprows, FALSE)) before returning vals$keeprows. See http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/validation.html for more on this powerful but unintuitive feature.

messages.subject: Authentication ideas for Shiny Server Pro
messages.subject_clean: Authentication ideas for Shiny Server Pro
messages.body_plain:
Hello Shiny community ~

So here's the situation ... I've got a PHP (and MSSQL/MySQL) based portal that my users log into.  Easy peasy, no issues there.  Because of the flexibility of PHP, we can authenticate with LDAP and provide access to particular services based on group membership etc.

Now with Shiny Server, the goal is to seamlessly integrate Shiny apps into the portal, and I am really struggling to figure out how this can be done.

We have multiple authentication realms that are done round-robin-style with PHP.  And now the web portal and Shiny apps are styled the same.  The only thing I'm missing ... How can I integrate the two seamlessly so the user does not know any different that they are accessing a protected Shiny app, and how can I provide access to specific Shiny apps to only specific users?

Any ideas?

All feedback is greatly appreciated.  Anything to spark my poor little brain ...

Thanks!
~Laz

> What's your intention with this code? Is keeprows supposed to stay up to date as mydata changes? Or is it supposed to just run a single time at startup? If so, at the time this code is running, are you sure mydata() is going to return something sensible (I suspect not as mydata requires a file upload)?
>
> I'll assume that you want to prepopulate keeprows each time a new file is uploaded. Then you'll do something like this:
>
> vals <- reactiveValues(
>   keeprows = NULL
> )
> observe({
>   vals$keeprows <- rep(TRUE, nrow(mydata()))
> })
>
> Also add this line to the beginning of the mydata reactive:
>
> validate(need(input$file, FALSE))
>
> The validate/need call will cause any code that calls mydata() to silently/cleanly abort if the file hasn't been uploaded yet (i.e. your outputs will be blank, without any error).
>
> The observer will cause keeprows to stay up to date.
>
> The one edge case you may still hit, is if an observer or renderXXX accesses vals$keeprows without first accessing mydata(). You can either check for NULL in those cases (or better yet, validate(need(vals$keeprows, FALSE)) ) or wrap the access to vals$keeprows in a reactive that calls validate(need(vals$keeprows, FALSE)) before returning vals$keeprows. Hello,

I am currently building a quite extensive shiny app using the shinydashboard package. After adding dozens of boxes and UI elements, an odd behavior showed up:

Single elements would simply not appear, while debug prints proved that the HTML code of the element was correctly assigned to the corresponding output handlers.

It gets even funnier: when I shortened the name of the element in question, it  finally appeared in the UI , but just for making another random element within a random menu item disappear.

I discovered also that the option 'outputOptions(output, "myElementID", suspendWhenHidden = FALSE)' helped for a single element in a similar manner, but also let the next random element disappear.

I hoped when setting suspendWhenHidden to FALSE for each and every element, shiny would realize that I am serious about my wish to render stuff, but it did not help.

So my questions are:

Is there a hard limit of the number of handlers in my output-list that shiny can handle?
If yes, how could I increase the limit?
If no, what else could be the problem, is it maybe my browsers fault?

Thanks in advance to all the knowledgable and talented shiny coders here in this forum...

> Single elements would simply not appear, while debug prints proved that the HTML code of the element was correctly assigned to the corresponding output handlers.
>
> It gets even funnier: when I shortened the name of the element in question, it  finally appeared in the UI , but just for making another random element within a random menu item disappear.
>
> I discovered also that the option 'outputOptions(output, "myElementID", suspendWhenHidden = FALSE)' helped for a single element in a similar manner, but also let the next random element disappear.
>
> I hoped when setting suspendWhenHidden to FALSE for each and every element, shiny would realize that I am serious about my wish to render stuff, but it did not help.
>
> So my questions are:
>
> Is there a hard limit of the number of handlers in my output-list that shiny can handle?
> If yes, how could I increase the limit?
> If no, what else could be the problem, is it maybe my browsers fault?
>
> Thanks in advance to all the knowledgable and talented shiny coders here in this forum...
>

messages.body_plain:
To answer your last question: I don't think you need the original path from your local computer, it sounds like perhaps the function you're using just needs the file to have its original filename (including extension).  When you upload a file using fileInput, the names of the file after being uploaded are NOT the same as the name of the file on your computer, so I sometimes use this bit of code to rename the uploaded files to match their real filenames.  Maybe this is all you need.

#' When files get uploaded, their new filenames are gibberish.
#' This function renames all uploaded files to their original names
#' @param x The dataframe returned from a shiny::fileInput
fixUploadedFilesNames <- function(x) {
 if (is.null(x)) {
   return()
 }

 oldNames = x$datapath
 newNames = file.path(dirname(x$datapath),
                      x$name)
 file.rename(from = oldNames, to = newNames)
 x$datapath <- newNames
 x
}

I’m a math grad student who is just started learning R, and I could really use some help from any R-literate people!!

I’m building a Shiny app that models probabilistic evolutionary dynamics (as a Markov process).
It can bee seen (in showcase mode) at:

+ https://amohseni.shinyapps.io/Moran-Process

THE PROBLEM: The simulation portion of the app is throwing out 2 errors that I haven’t figured out. They are as follows:

When population size N is small (N<10) it often (but not always) throws

Error: in sample.int <http://sample.int>(length(x), size, replace, prob) :
  incorrect number of probabilities

When population size N is large (N>100) it often (but not always) throws

Error: in sample.int <http://sample.int>(length(x), size, replace, prob) :
  non-positive probability

You can replicate this error by setting the populations slider to max (200) or min (0),
and clicking “Simulate Single Population” repeatedly until you get an error.

It seems likely that the problem stems from this chunk of code:

    MPM.sim <- function(t, MPM, πNought) {
# The simulation function takes as arguments: duration t, the MPM matrix of transition probabilities, and some initial condition πNought
      sim <- as.numeric(t)
      if (missing(πNought)) { # If the initial state is not specified
        sim[1] <- (sample(1:(N+1),1) - 1) # Then take a random initial state
      }else{sim[1]<-πNought} # If the initial state is specified, start from that state.
      for(i in 2:t){ # For each step of the simulation after the initial state,
        newstate <- sample(1:(N+1),1,prob=MPM[sim[i-1],]) # The transition to the next state is given by the transition matrix MPM.
        sim[i] <- newstate
      }
      sim
    }

I would be tremendously appreciative of any help or suggestions!

messages.subject: Rendering an image from Amazon Web Services S3
messages.subject_clean: Rendering an image from Amazon Web Services S3
messages.body_plain:
I am currently able to display a logo on a shinyapp using the following:

  output$image1 <- renderImage( {
    filename <- "logo.gif"
    return(list(
      src = filename,
      filetype = "image/gif"
    ))
  }, deleteFile=FALSE)

In the above case, the file is a local file.

I would like to create an app that allows the user to display images from a non-public S3 bucket on AWS.

I am somewhat new to interfacing with S3, and I am currently using the aws.s3 and aws.signature libraries.

I am able to display the contents of a bucket using:

library(aws.s3)
library(aws.signature)

getB <- function() {
  a <- aws.s3::getbucket(bucket = "bucketname",
                         key = "mykey",
                         secret = "mySecret"
  )
  summary(a)
}

and

output$text1 <- renderText({ getB() })

I am not sure of the next step.  Does an image have to be saved locally, before being displayed?  Can it be displayed directly by giving the file path (e.g.  https://s3.amazonaws.com/bucketname/logo.gif)?  I have tried this but it does not work.
